chapter: Bill Robinson and Chuck and Chuckles
title: The pool game against Bill Robinson with Don Redmond
summary: At the Rhythm Club Green partnered Don Redmond against Robinson at pool, with Baby Lawrence nearby, and banked the last ball to win.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Baby Lawrence, and he used to take us to the gaming room, and he was teaching us how to shoot pool, how to play position with the cue ball. In other words, how to run the largest amount of balls. You have to put them in the pockets. And they were considered as points. Well, Mr. Bill Bojangles Robinson, he would like to wager, you see, so he figured that Mr. Don Redmond, being a band leader, the orchestra leader, and famous, with the (Unintelligible), the jazz giants, you see, he would make a wager. He would give odds. He said he -- "How many points do you want?" he'd say. "I'll allow you 25 points and I'll play you and whatever partner you would choose 500 points, see? So naturally, the little giant, he chose his student, which was me. So that evening, Mr. Baby Lawrence, I think he was invited as some kind of celebrity. He had to be a celebrity up in a nightclub, an after hours club that was called Dickie Wells'. So we started to play in this -- see, this game points is -- you have to -- whoever gets the cue ball the closest from one cushion to the other, lengthwise, they wouldn't have to break the balls, see? And so we did that. He said he would break the balls. He was also spiting us there. Well now, Don Redmond was an expert. He was really a champion pool player, you know. He shot billiards. And he could make the cue ball actually talk, you see. And he could play one ball and he's in position to play the next ball and so forth and so on. Now, it was up to he and

I to make 475 points. So what happened is Mr. Bill Bojangles Robinson, he broke the balls and it was very safe. There didn't seem like there was any way of making a ball, pocketing a ball, you see. But, as I say, Mr. Don Redmond, he was a teacher, see, and very expert in this art. So he saw a ball he could pocket, and also opened a ball where he would get the other balls closer to the pocket, see? So that's what he done. And he started to shooting, he run up to 444 balls before he would miss. When he would miss a ball, he would leave Bill Bojangles Robinson kind of what they call hid. He couldn't find a shot, you see. So he'd have to expose the cue ball or play safe, see? And in order to play safe you have to hit one ball and make one ball go to the cushion. It could either be the ball you hit or the cue ball, you see, as long as you hide the cue ball where the competitor wouldn't have a chance to pocket a ball, see, a point. So the highlight of the game is that you have to bank the last point, see, so somehow it happened there that the play got tighter and tighter, see. I didn't get a chance to run but 19 of the balls, you see, but they was all easy shots, because Mr. Don Redmond had taught me how to do this. You make one ball and make the other balls get closer to the pocket, so you could pocket them. And it was always 15 balls in a rack, and that's what happened. I banked the last ball, you see.
